question: What does Grok Imagine actually return on three locked briefs, and which other estate image APIs can we run today?
configVsRuntime: Tool results reported model grok-imagine-image (fast), not grok-imagine-image-quality. Config is not proof of the quality route.

lockedPrompts.prompt: A single matte-black machined cylinder, about 12 centimeters tall, with one hairline gold ring at the midsection, standing alone on a dark slate desk. Warm sidelight from camera left, soft falloff, shallow depth of field, photoreal product photograph, 16:9. No logos, no readable text, no watermarks, no people, no screens, no UI.

An empty reading room at dusk: one oak table, one empty wooden chair, a tall window with cool blue twilight, an unlit brass lamp on the table, architectural photograph, 35mm lens, natural materials, quiet atmosphere, 16:9. No logos, no readable text, no book titles, no people, no watermarks.

A small cute modern 3D droid with compact chibi proportions, smooth cream polymer shell, a simple pixel-dot face made of two dots and a short arc, standing on a pale seamless studio floor, soft even light, collectible product render, 16:9. No humans, no skeletal robots, no logos, no readable text, no watermarks.

backends.costField: cost_in_usd_ticks=200000000 per call; dollar conversion not documented in this session

outputs.notes: Subject matches. Gold ring present. No text/people. Upper half reads warmer bronze than matte black.
Two chairs instead of one. Brass lamp shade reads lit, prompt asked unlit. No people or readable titles.
Cute cream figure with two dots and an arc. Reads more as a blob mascot than a mechanical droid. No humans, text, or skeletal forms.
